reason: The cited evidence (E1) states that binder jetting/ink-extrusion with isothermal sintering can provide segregation-free, homogeneous alloys with low residual stress due to full inter-diffusion, supporting the first three premises. However, E1 does not mention AlCrFeNiSi or any specific high-entropy alloy, so the applicability to this specific material system is assumed rather than evidenced. The feasibility of low-temperature sintering for full densification of this alloy without oxidation or phase formation is also not addressed in the cited passage.
premises: Binder-based AM with isothermal sintering yields segregation-free, homogeneous alloys with low residual stress.
Full inter-diffusion during isothermal sintering eliminates compositional gradients.
The process avoids rapid temperature gradients and high cooling rates that cause segregation and residual stress.
The cited evidence applies to AlCrFeNiSi or similar high-entropy alloys.
Low-temperature sintering can fully densify AlCrFeNiSi without oxidation or unwanted phases.
